---
title: "Why does checking my bank balance feel like bracing for bad news — even when I know it's fine?"
pubDate: 2026-07-17
description: "You earn well. You save. You still open the banking app with your jaw slightly tight. That's not a personality flaw. It's a pattern with a name."
tags: ["money vigilance", "financial behaviour", "money scripts"]
---

You earn decent money. You probably have a savings buffer. You check your balance anyway — maybe twice before lunch — and for a second, every time, there's a small clench before the number loads.

When the number is fine, you feel relieved for about forty seconds. Then the tab is still open.

This is not anxiety in the clinical sense. It is a learned posture. At some point, staying watchful felt like the responsible thing to do, and it worked well enough that you never questioned whether you could stop.

The problem is not that you're careful with money. The problem is that careful has become constant, and constant doesn't feel like safety. It feels like waiting.

Joel here. MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner. I work with people who are good with money on paper and exhausted by it in practice. The pattern above has a name in the research — money vigilance — and understanding what it is doing for you (not to you) is where the work underneath the spreadsheet starts.

If you want to see where your own patterns sit, the quiz takes four minutes. No score to dread. Just a clearer picture of the story beneath the money.
